writeup: TIC 389751698 is a candidate eclipsing binary star detected in TESS photometry data with an orbital period of 21.289427 days. The primary eclipse produces a 19.54% dimming, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal reached a detection significance of 142.3 in the automated search pipeline, and pixel-level analysis confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 34.6, though the centroid offset of 3.4 arcseconds warrants attention. The target does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. One important caveat exists: the automated analysis initially reported a shorter 10.6447-day period, but a data quality check revealed that alternating eclipses differ significantly in depth, indicating the true period is double the initially reported value. The machine-learning screening score of 0.21 reflects moderate confidence in this candidate.
